summary: Iteration 4 review PASSED end-to-end. Backend: 11/11 pytest tests green (5 new + 6 preserved). Frontend: 23/23 mobile-viewport UI assertions green against the deployed preview URL. Verified: (1) POST /api/upload with Bearer token accepts a real PNG and returns {path, url}; the returned /api/files/{path} GET responds 200 with content-type image/*; POST /api/upload without token -> 401/403; text/plain payload -> 400. (2) POST /api/owner/stores accepts logo_url+banner_url and persists them (GET /api/stores/{id} returns the same). PUT /api/owner/stores/{id} updates logo_url/banner_url and persists. Product image_url persists on POST and PUT (visible in public /api/stores/{id}/products). (3) Home ordering pins premium/is_featured first (first store card = store_3 which is premium; 2 vip-badge-* elements visible). (4) Profile role-scoped menu is exactly as required: consumer sees only profile-goto-favorites-btn (no owner/admin), owner sees profile-goto-owner-dashboard-btn + profile-goto-plans-btn (no admin/favorites), admin sees profile-goto-admin-btn only. profile-open-role-switcher-btn present for all 3 roles. (5) Upload UI presence + clickability: edit-store-profile-btn opens modal with edit-store-logo-picker + edit-store-banner-picker (both clickable); owner-new-store-btn opens modal with new-store-logo-picker + new-store-banner-picker; owner catalog add-new-product-btn opens modal with product-image-picker. All legacy testIDs preserved.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py is >1240 lines - consider splitting routers (auth, stores, owner, admin, media) into separate modules to stay under the 700-line guideline.

GET /api/files/{file_path:path} is intentionally public (marketplace assets). If in the future users upload private/sensitive images via this same endpoint, add per-namespace ACLs or a signed-URL layer.

api.uploadImage returns `${BACKEND_URL}${data.url}` (absolute URL) but the backend also stores the relative path. Persist the relative /api/files/... path (not the absolute one) to remain host-agnostic across environments; verify frontend callers do this on save (dashboard/catalog persistence).
